newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- An eight-year-old illegal immigrant girl and her mother were forcibly deported to China. Most Hong Kong residents thought the government was justified in doing so.

-- SING TAO -- A war among gangsters in the Portuguese-run enclave of Macau near Hong Kong escalated as two people were killed in a shooting and 12 youths were wounded in a knife attack at a video game parlour.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin is scheduled to meet Russian leader Boris Yeltsin today as the two nations discuss the formation of a new partnership.

-- Talking about China's efforts to join the World Trade Organisation, Premier Li Peng urging WTO members to understand the realities of China's economic development and to avoid politicising the issue.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- An increasing number of Western-educated mainland Chinese young professionals had come to Hong Kong to assist local enterprises in developing the Chinese market.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The government has devised a plan to push through controversial changes to a proposed pension plan, the Mandatory Provident Fund, in an attempt to ensure the legislation is passed before the territory's handover to China on July 1.
-- Some of the most important Chinese bankers in the territory have formed an exclusive club to organise a handover party for the financial services industry.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD --The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong was set to release an extended list of securities for short-selling, following consultation with the Securities and Futures Commission.
-- Hong Kong's inflation rate fell to 5.9 percent year-on-year in March, thanks to a decline in the price of some food items.
